By this award, the instant claim petition under section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
filed by LRs of deceased Amar Singh, who died in a motor vehicular accident occurred on 26.10.2019 at near Vandana Nagar (Near Ankur Vihar DLF), Vijay Vihar within the jurisdiction of PS Tronika City, Distt. Ghaziabad, U.P. has been decided in connection with the accident, FIR no.
648/2019, under Sections 279/338/304A IPC was registered at PS Tronika City, Distt. Ghaziabad,
U.P.

Briefly stated the facts as mentioned in the petition are that on 26.10.2019 Amar Singh (since Deceased) was going towards Kudedan from his house on foot.

When he reached near Vandana Nagar (Near Ankur Vihar DLF), Vijay Vihar within the jurisdiction of PS Tronika City, Distt.
Ghaziabad, U.P., in the meantime, a motorcycle bearing registration No. DL-5SAR-0722 (TVS Kiran vs Jitender Kumar@Jeetu on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4534555/
1 Apache) which was being driven by its driver at a very high speed, rashly negligently, without taking necessary precautions, without proper lookouts, violating the traffic rules, zig-zag manner and without blowing any horn came and hit Amar Singh with a great force.
As a result of which, Amar Singh fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Community Health Center, Loni, Ghaziabad, where first aid given to him and thereafter he was referred to GTB Hospital, Dilshad Garden, Delhi, where he died during treatment on 01.11.2019.
With these submissions, petitioners have claimed a compensation of Rs. 40 lakh alongwith interest @ 12% per annum from the respondent.
3. Vide order dated 18.11.2022, respondent was proceeded ex- parte as he did not appear and did not file his written statement.

4. In order to establish their case, petitioners led their evidence and examined two witnesses as under :
4.1. Petitioner no. 1 examined herself as PW1, who is wife of the deceased.
PW-2 Vijay Kumar was an eyewitness of the case.
He tendered his affidavit Ex.PW1/A and and relied upon copy of his Aadhar card as Ex.PW2/1.
No other witness has been examined and ex-parte PE was closed vide order dt. 23.08.2024.

5. Statement of petitioner no. 1 was also recorded as per Clause 29 of MCTAP on 08.01.2025,
wherein she stated that her husband late Amar Singh died in a road accident on 01.11.2019 at about 9:35 p.m.
He was about 49 years old at the time of his death.

Deceased was doing private job at Bunglow No. 1, Chadrawal Water Works, 1, Behind Vidhan Sabha, Civil Lines, Delhi and was earning about Rs. 18,000/- to Rs. 25,000/- p.m.
6.
I have heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the petitioners and perused the evidence and other material placed on record.
7. It is settled law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
8.

When he reached near Vandana Nagar (Near Ankur Vihar DLF)
Vijay Vihar within the jurisdiction of PS Tronika City, Distt Ghaziabad, he got down from the TSR,
in the meanwhile he saw a motorcycle bearing registration No.DL-5SAR-0722 (TVS Apache), which was being driven by its driver, a a very high speed, rashly, negligently, without taking, zig- zag manner and without blowing any horn came from Delhi side and hit Amar Singh with a great force.
He further deposed that as a result of which, he fall down on the road and sustained/grievous injuries.
Thereafter public gathered at the spot and police came at the spot and injured was removed to the hospital.
Thereafter he came to know that Amar Singh died during the course of treatment on 01.11.2019 at 09:35 p.m. PW-2
further deposed that this accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending motor cycle bearing registration No.DL-5SAR-0722.
Police recorded his statement EX.PW2/2 regarding this accident.

He further deposed that had the motorcycle driver been careful and cautious enough this accident could have been averted and the deceased would not had died an unnatural and untimely death in the accident.

she categorically stated that accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent, who was driving the offending vehicle.
10. It is seen that the aforesaid ocular testimonies of the witnesses remained unchallenged and uncontroverted from the side of respondent.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimonies of PW-1 and PW-2, more particularly the testimony of eye-witness (PW2) made on oath.

Moreover, the ocular testimonies of the witnesses are also corroborated by documentary evidence brought on record i.e. certified copies of FIR, charge-sheet, etc.
11.
The certified copy of the FIR shows that description/ registration number of the offending vehicle (motorcycle) has been clearly mentioned in the FIR.
On perusal of criminal case record, it is found that the offending vehicle was being driven by the respondent at the time of accident in question.
12. Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and charge sheet has also been filed against the respondent by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent was negligent.
Reliance is placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v. Satvir & Ors.

MAC. APP. 980/17 dated 24.01.2020 , wherein Hon'ble Delhi High Court observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of accident having been caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioners have been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that the death of deceased due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent.

16. In view of the above findings, it has come on record that accident occurred due to rash negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the respondent and thus, it has been been established on record that there was composite negligence on the part of respondent in causing the accident.
Now the real issue is to determine the extent of liability of the offending vehicle.

It has come in the evidence of eye-witness (PW2) that he was present at the spot and saw that offending motorcycle, being driven by the respondent in a high speed, rashly and negligently came and hit the deceased and as a result of the impact of accident, the deceased sustained injuries and he received grievous injuries and taken to hospital and during treatment he died in the hospital.

The manner of accident as testified by the eye-witness clearly shows that the motorcycle was being driven at a high speed, rashly and negligently and accident occurred, which indicates that the motorcycle was at a high speed.
Had the motorcycle was not being driven at a high speed, it could have successfully applied the brakes and deceased could have been saved.

Thus, it is concluded that the driver i.e. respondent was at fault and accordingly, it is held that liability is of the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

17. On the basis of findings as above, it is established on record that the incident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no.1, resulting into death of deceased.
Hence, it is held that petitioners are entitled to get the compensation in this case.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.

6 Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.

Step-3 (Actual Calculation) The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family."12.

"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
7. It is settled law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
8.
Thus, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimonies of PW-1 and PW-2, more particularly the testimony of eye-witness (PW2) made on oath.
Moreover, the ocular testimonies of the witnesses are also corroborated by documentary evidence brought on record i.e. certified copies of FIR, charge-sheet, etc.
11.
The certified copy of the FIR shows that description/ registration number of the offending vehicle (motorcycle) has been clearly mentioned in the FIR.
On perusal of criminal case record, it is found that the offending vehicle was being driven by the respondent at the time of accident in question.
12. Thus, the facts that FIR has been registered and charge sheet has also been filed against the respondent by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent was negligent.

Not only this, the respondent (driver-cum-owner of offending vehicle) was also the material witness, who could have thrown light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances, the accident had taken place.
However, he preferred not to enter into witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Ins. Co. Ltd. vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 18. Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
Petitioners not claimed any medical expenses for treatment of deceased before his death as the deceased was immediately taken to Community Health Centre, Loni Ghaziabad, where first aid was given to him and thereafter he was referred to GTB Hospital where he died during course of treatment on 01.11.2019.
Therefore, no amount is granted to the petitioners under this head.
In Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, the relevant guidelines were laid down for death cases, which have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs.
Pranay Sethi & Ors.
Therefore, the income of deceased has to be considered at par with minimum wages applicable to unskilled category of workers in Delhi at the relevant time.
The minimum wages of an unskilled person in Delhi on the date of accident i.e. 26.10.2019, were Rs.14,842/- p.m.
Thus, the income of the deceased would be considered to be Rs.14,842/- per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
Deductions out of earning of the Number of deceased dependents Where dependent is 1 Half Where the number of dependent 1/3rd family members is 2 to 3 Where the number of dependent 1/4th family members is 4 to 6 Where the number of dependent 1/5th family members exceeds 6 (six)
